name: Loki's Castle

sources.title: Pedersen et al. (2010), Discovery of a black smoker vent field and vent fauna at the Arctic Mid-Ocean Ridge, Nature Communications 1: four black smokers up to 13 m on sulphide mounds 150-200 m across, 310-320 °C, Sclerolinum tubeworm fields
Loki's Castle — about 2,352 m, where the Mohns and Knipovich ridges meet
Scientific Reports (2023) — the western and eastern mounds of the Loki's Castle vent field and their fauna
Live Science — In photos: Norway's spooky seafloor vents (bacterial mats on the chimneys)

notes: Built by code (model_sources/Q6668666_lokis_castle.py, tools/meshkit.py, tools/scenekit.py) with AI assistance. One sulphide mound about 200 m across and 25 m high, black and rust-brown, with two vent sites: at each, two active black-smoker chimneys of 9-13 m with beehive ledges and white bacterial dusting near the top, and smaller extinct or diffuse chimneys about them. The shape of the mound and of each chimney, and the distance between the vent sites, are approximate. No marine life in the model: Offlined draws the living things itself.
